why:
The finding is real. In book-2.json the 經 of 二·六 (有待, rendered 二·五) is the only 經 before 十一·二 that uses 应 in the sense of response. 篇八 uses 应 too, but only in 相应, the separate name for the hexagram relation. 应 is defined at 十一·二 (rendered 十一·一), nine parts later, so this 經 does not rest on earlier 條.

It is also the wrong name, not just an early one. NAMES-ZH anchors 应 to `ExchangeLaw.RespondsTo` (LevelCoupling.lean line 110): two histories that differ in one level give a positive exchange gap. That is an existence claim. What this 經 reads is `ExchangeRelation.RespondsBelow` (ExchangePremises.lean lines 597–601): under every history that differs only in c's level at t, with that level below n, no admitted exchange has f exchange. RespondsBelow does not imply RespondsTo: a formation that never exchanges satisfies RespondsBelow vacuously but has zero gap. So 必然之应 is not a 应 in the book's sense.

The parentheses in the 經 already state both readings in full, using only names defined earlier. `MayRespondBelow` (lines 603–605: under every such history some admitted exchange leaves f idle) matches 或 as defined at 凡·四: some open branch holds, and you can say which. RespondsBelow matches 必 at 凡·四: every open branch holds. So 必无取与 and 或无取与 say exactly what the Lean says.

The reviewer's find occurs exactly once in the 二·六 body and is used unchanged. Left as they are, and acceptable: the 說 keeps 必然之应 and 可能之应 next to the Lean names, as the current Chinese edition's gloss, and the 篇二 intro uses 必然之应 in modern prose. One optional extra: the 說's pointer 应见⟦十一·二⟧ could say that RespondsBelow is not an instance of 应 there.
